# 九色鹿經

**ID:** T0181a
**Volume:** T03
**Category:** 本緣部類
**Original Category:** 本緣部
**Byline:** 吳 支謙譯
**Dynasty:** 吳
**Date:** 223–253
**Juans:** 1

## Contributors
- 支謙 (A000164)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short single-fascicle *jātaka* recounting the past life of the Buddha as a *Bodhisattva-deer* with nine-coloured fur and snow-white antlers, who rescues a drowning man from the Ganges; the man, betraying his oath, reports the deer's whereabouts to the queen who covets its skin. Translated by [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) Zhī Qiān in the Wú. Signature: 「吳月氏優婆塞支謙譯」. The Taishō header cross-references [T152(58)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0001).

The *Nine-Coloured Deer* narrative is one of the most widely-attested *jātaka*s in East-Asian Buddhist art, painted in the Mògāo Cave 257 (Northern-Wèi period) at Dūnhuáng — one of the masterpieces of medieval Chinese Buddhist mural painting.

**Abstract**

T181a is the *Korean*-canon recension of [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) Zhī Qiān's translation; [T181b](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0036) is a parallel recension of the same translation in slightly different textual state. The Indic source corresponds to the *Ruru-jātaka* (Pāli *Jātaka* no. 482), known in Sanskrit as the *Ruru-mṛga-jātaka* and depicted at Bharhut, Sānchī, and most famously in the Ajaṇṭā Cave 17 mural cycle.
